content.intro: Learn load testing and capacity planning through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Load Testing and Capacity Planning matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines load testing and capacity planning as part of performance, caching, and scalability. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

items.text: Async code helps most when it can await non-blocking I/O; CPU-heavy work or blocking libraries can still stall the event loop. Test timeouts, cancellation, concurrency limits, and sync/async boundaries.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
